summary: scripts/st-test (fractal-test) counts a check as signed, for a tree that edits a file that decides skipping, only on a note at the gate's own levels (host), asking the verifier for the newest pass at those levels as the gate does. A note CI signed for the same inputs no longer reads as 'already signed', so st-test signs the check on the host instead of leaving CI to refuse it.

replay.detail: No record, signature or verifier rule changes; the gate is unchanged.

schema.detail: No stored or wire format changes.

rules.detail: st-test's 'already signed' and --status 'covered' follow the gate's own_pull_request rule for protected-file trees: only a note at the base gate's OWN_LEVELS covers them. PROTECTED and OWN_LEVELS are read from the base's scripts/ci-evidence-gate, so the two cannot drift.

compatibility.detail: A tree that edits no protected file is judged as before. A base gate without PROTECTED or OWN_LEVELS keeps the old behaviour.

manual.detail: None; a protected-file branch may now run a check locally that st-test used to skip.
